--- pc1.startup ---
#!/bin/sh
set -eu
# Kathara: interfacce gia attive, solo IPv4 e routing statico.
ip -4 address show dev eth0 | grep -Fq 'inet 10.14.1.11/24 ' || ip address add 10.14.1.11/24 dev eth0

ip route replace default via 10.14.1.1 dev eth0

# ARP statico limitato ai vicini sul medesimo dominio L2.
ip -4 neigh replace 10.14.1.1 lladdr 02:00:00:0a:01:01 nud permanent dev eth0
ip -4 neigh replace 10.14.1.12 lladdr 02:00:00:0a:01:03 nud permanent dev eth0
ip -4 neigh replace 10.14.1.13 lladdr 02:00:00:0a:01:04 nud permanent dev eth0
ip -4 neigh replace 10.14.1.14 lladdr 02:00:00:0a:01:05 nud permanent dev eth0

# Stabilizzazione del gateway (massimo 8 tentativi, mai fatale).
probe_attempt=0
while [ "$probe_attempt" -lt 8 ]; do
    if ping -n -I eth0 -c 1 -W 1 10.14.1.1 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        break
    fi
    probe_attempt=$((probe_attempt + 1))
    [ "$probe_attempt" -lt 8 ] || break
    sleep 1
done

item.text: The lab already has IPv4 routes between all six LANs and enough hosts for separate DNS roles. I’ll use an artificial root, delegated zones, and one recursive resolver; the requested mail destinations will receive MX records.

/usr/bin/bash -lc "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
roles = {
 'pc1': ('.','a.root-servers.', '10.14.1.11', [('com','ns.com.','10.14.1.12'),('net','ns.net.','10.14.1.13')], []),
 'pc2': ('com','ns.com.','10.14.1.12',[('example','ns.example.com.','10.14.3.13'),('service','ns.service.com.','10.14.4.14')],[]),
 'pc3': ('net','ns.net.','10.14.1.13',[('lab','ns.lab.net.','10.14.5.11'),('tools','ns.tools.net.','10.14.5.13')],[]),
 'pc10': ('example.com','ns.example.com.','10.14.3.13',[],['shop IN A 10.14.3.11','mail IN A 10.14.1.14','@ IN MX 10 mail.example.com.']),
 'pc14': ('service.com','ns.service.com.','10.14.4.14',[],['api IN A 10.14.3.12','mail IN A 10.14.2.11','@ IN MX 10 mail.service.com.']),
 'pc15': ('lab.net','ns.lab.net.','10.14.5.11',[('research','ns.research.lab.net.','10.14.5.12')],['mail IN A 10.14.2.12','@ IN MX 10 mail.lab.net.']),
 'pc16': ('research.lab.net','ns.research.lab.net.','10.14.5.12',[],['ai IN A 10.14.4.12','data IN A 10.14.4.13']),
 'pc17': ('tools.net','ns.tools.net.','10.14.5.13',[],['ci IN A 10.14.4.11','mail IN A 10.14.2.13','@ IN MX 10 mail.tools.net.']),
}
for dev,(zone,ns,ip,delegations,records) in roles.items():
    d=Path(dev)/'etc/bind'; d.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
    filename='db.root' if zone=='.' else 'db.'+zone
    (d/'named.conf').write_text('options { directory \"/var/cache/bind\"; recursion no; allow-query { any; }; dnssec-validation no; listen-on { any; }; listen-on-v6 { any; }; };\\nzone \"'+zone+'\" { type master; file \"/etc/bind/'+filename+'\"; };\\n')
    hostmaster='hostmaster.' if zone=='.' else 'hostmaster.'+zone+'.'
    lines=['"'$TTL 3600'"',f'@ IN SOA {ns} {hostmaster} ( 1 3600 900 604800 300 )',f'@ IN NS {ns}',f'{ns} IN A {ip}']
    for label,target,addr in delegations:
        lines += [f'{label} IN NS {target}',f'{target} IN A {addr}']
    lines += records
    (d/filename).write_text('\\n'.join(lines)+'\\n')
    with Path(dev+'.startup').open('a') as f: f.write('\\nsystemctl restart named\\n')
d=Path('pc18/etc/bind'); d.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
(d/'named.conf').write_text('options { directory \"/var/cache/bind\"; recursion yes; allow-recursion { any; }; allow-query { any; }; dnssec-validation no; listen-on { any; }; listen-on-v6 { any; }; };\\nzone \".\" { type hint; file \"/etc/bind/db.hints\"; };\\n')
(d/'db.hints').write_text('. 3600000 IN NS a.root-servers.\\na.root-servers. 3600000 IN A 10.14.1.11\\n')
with Path('pc18.startup').open('a') as f: f.write('\\nsystemctl restart named\\n')
for n in range(1,21):
    p=Path(f'pc{n}.startup')
    with p.open('a') as f: f.write('\\necho \"nameserver 10.14.6.11\" > /etc/resolv.conf\\n')
PY"

item.text:
Configured DNS for the requested hostnames and MX records, using the existing IPv4 addresses and connections. All 20 PCs use the recursive resolver on **pc18**.

The artificial root is on pc1; pc2 and pc3 serve `.com` and `.net`; pc10, pc14, pc15, pc16 and pc17 serve the delegated domains. The DNS configuration files and PC startup scripts were updated; no images were changed.

The mail records identify pc4, pc5, pc6 and pc7 as requested. They do not configure mail server software. Runtime validation was not performed, and the local BIND checking utilities were unavailable.
